## THE PIECE (context)
**"YOUR UPDATE HAS FAILED."** — a browser + WebXR (Quest 3) piece: one computer across four eras dramatizes
how conversion-practice ("SOGICE") networks targeting queer people evolved — the demand never changes, only
the disguise. Built and shipped: Eras 1–3 (a teen/1997, an ex-gay man "Daniel"/2003, a lesbian "Story
Steward" Vera/2016), plus a designed-but-unbuilt Era 4 (a trans woman, "Maya"/present, closing the piece with
a warm-glitch climax, "TRANSCENDANCE"). Hard rails that govern everything, no exceptions: no runtime
network/storage; click/tap-only (VR-safe, no timer/reflex/score/streak/win-lose except satirizing the SYSTEM
gamifying selfhood); all display text in `data/` JSON; invented composites only, real people/orgs cited in a
hidden documentary panel only, never played; satire targets the apparatus, never queer people/survivors;
detransition is legitimate and never vilified; a working Leave/pause reachable from every scene.

Since 2026-07-01, a reinterpretation thread has been exploring a structural redesign: instead of one
composite person per era, each era becomes a **radial cluster** — one identity's room lit/foregrounded
(gay man / lesbian woman / trans man / trans woman), the other three as dimmed peripheral alcoves — plus a
scattered layer of **"provotypes"**: small, deliberately unwinnable interactive vignettes (some new, some
already-existing, like the ad-game ZAP!) dramatizing real documented SOGICE techniques, where the
unwinnability is the argument: **even played as the enforcer, the person's queerness/transness always
survives** — the glitch doctrine, as a mechanic.

change → files/keys touched → guardrails). Cover at minimum:

### 4. One consolidated ethics/trans-reader gate list
Gather every "requires ethics/trans-reader consult" flag scattered across the reading list (there are
several, from different documents, covering overlapping and distinct content) into a single list, deduplicated,

### 5. The smallest coherent slice

whole direction works — one provotype, fully built, in context? Recommend which one and why, given the

**Built and committed** (`a005c39`) — your dolly design is implemented exactly as you described it, both side rooms are now full rooms, and the blocking furniture is out of the sightlines. And yes — your camera idea makes complete sense; it fixed the centering problem and the "surrounded by rooms" problem in one move.

## The dolly, as you specced it

The camera now lives in **seats** — one fixed, composed position per room, so inside a room the view is always centered: desk in front of you, the rest of the room around it. Moving between rooms is the dolly you described: **zoom out to the center of the space** (this is the moment you see all the rooms around you), **swing, zoom in** to the next room's desk. It triggers three ways:

- **Turn your head** (drag) past a room's edge and let go — the camera follows the path to that room, exactly your "when the person turns their head it follows the path of the camera."
- **Arrow keys** step room to room the same way.
- **R** returns to the era's home room.

Grabbing the view mid-travel cancels it, and releasing re-seats you at the nearest room, so you can never get stranded. THE TURN at Era 4 is now the dolly at its heaviest: pull back through the center of thirty years of rooms, swing 180°, settle at Maya's desk with the lamp and the record. In VR none of this applies — your head is the camera and the rooms simply surround you.

## The rooms and the limiters

- **Both side rooms are full rooms now**, built from one bedroom template at the lead room's density: framed curtained window, posters, headboard bed, four-legged desk, era devices (chunky '03 CRT + tape deck + pamphlets in the west; laptop + webcam + misfiled folders + the dark phone in the east, with the niche as that room's wall furniture). I verified every seat's framing by screenshot — each one reads as a centered room. Two framing bugs were caught and fixed in the process (seats initially sat too deep, inside the monitors).
- **The tall bookcase and wardrobe that blocked your views are gone from the middle** — tall pieces now stand flat against the angled rim walls between rooms, only chest-height runs sit near the center, and the rooms' own beds bound the rear. You always see over and past the limits into the neighboring rooms.

## The asset research you asked for

I ran the agent; the verdict is clean: **Kenney's Furniture Kit** — CC0, and crucially its models use *flat solid-color materials with no textures*, so it fits our "no textures, palette-only" law with a simple recolor in code. The plan it recommends: kit models for hero furniture only (beds, desks, chairs, wardrobes), boxes stay for background pieces, and PlayCanvas's batcher merges everything — which drops all static furniture to **~6–10 draw calls**, finally solving the Quest ≤60 law at the same time as the visual upgrade. Your JSON editing workflow survives: a room entry just says `"model": "bed_double"` instead of a box size. This is one focused session; say yes and it's the next thing built.

## What to check live

Run `?reinterp=1&era=2&debug=1`: drag past a room's edge and release, tap the arrows, press R — the dolly animations run at full speed only in your browser (my preview environment freezes animations, so I verified every end framing but the motion itself is your check). Then Era 4 for the TURN-as-dolly. One note: your dev server holds port 5174, so my sessions now auto-pick a free port — nothing you need to do.

Why this round exists (Sérgio's words, 2026-07-22)
"This has been so hard to track that even you got confused. This needs a better system."
He is right, and the evidence is concrete. In one session an agent read R28 §4's line "the cork panel as onboarding is dead" and then spent an hour refactoring that exact panel — then reported a long-known fact (dead code since Session 27) as a discovery, and invented a scope item ("Era 1 needs a rebuild") that appears in NO document. Two of the three errors were caught by Sérgio, not by tooling. The tracking failure is the subject of this round, not a footnote to it.
Verify every finding below against the files before you reconcile it. The agent that produced this brief was wrong twice in the same session; treat its claims as leads, not as record.
What actually shipped this session (verify, then fold into the plan)
Commit `ee70a2c` — enforcement + palette

* `tools/check-spec.mjs`, wired into `npm test`. Enforces four laws that were written down but not enforced: C1 dossier `status` + `confidence` on every provotype debrief source; C2 felt-scene purity (no assistant may offer a `register: felt` scene); C3 `tier`/`register` vocabulary + the ≤3-hero-per-scene Quest budget; C4 palette discipline as a ratchet (fails on growth, nags downward) rather than a hard fail.
* The gap it closed matters more than the tool: `CLAUDE.md` states the dossier status law is CI-enforced — "Build fails without it" — and `data/provotypes/_schema.json` repeats the claim. Neither was true. `npm test` never read `data/provotypes/`. A law documented as enforced and not enforced is worse than an unwritten one. Assume this is not the only instance; finding the others is part of this round.
* New `src/desktop/theme/board.ts` + `theme/witness.ts`. Hardcoded colors outside `theme/`: 157 → 51. Pure naming pass, proven value-preserving (identical color multiset vs HEAD). One token now carries meaning: `FLAG` (#cc8855) marks every refusal the record files.

Commit `d7053e6` — the Close as knowledge graph (schema + criteria only, nothing migrated)

* `data/strings/_close_network.schema.json` (proposed): nodes with `status` from the dossier vocabulary, edges with `relation ∈ grounds|informs|supersedes`, gated by one top-level `sergioPass` boolean.
* `tools/close-graph-report.mjs` — read-only, not in `npm test`.

Findings that need YOUR reconciliation (each is a decision, not a chore)

1. The deprecated cork onboarding is still live. R28 §4 killed the cork panel as onboarding and specified a three-layer replacement (orienting card / game menu / conductor teaches LOOK-MOVE- INTERACT). Layers 1–2 shipped in Session 36. Layer 3 did not, and `src/engine/app.ts` still calls `witness.setStartupBoard()` and `witness.handleStartupClick()` — so a fresh `?reinterp=1` shows the R28 replacement AND, one click later, the thing R28 declared dead. Nuance that matters: the board itself survives as the witness lineage's first state (MASTER_PLAN_v2: warm cork board → cold intake record → dashboards → Maya's wall → constellation). What died is the onboarding job — the "Start-up options / This screen / Headset / Conducted view" panel. Partition it.
2. `mountStartupOverlay()` in `src/desktop/opening.ts` (~440 lines) is called from nowhere — dead since Session 27, per the session log. Its header claims a future as the VR in-scene opening. Retire it, or keep it with a header stating it is unmounted and awaiting the VR port. Its copy keys in `data/strings/opening.json` are still live via `intake.ts` — the data file stays either way.
3. Every dossier source still carries `[VERIFY SOURCE]` — all 8 across both real provotypes. Per `CLAUDE.md` that means none is Sérgio-checked. This gates the constellation idea (no node may render as a bright documentary star yet) and is a standing ethics item that deserves a place on `07_WAITING_ON_SERGIO.md` with an honest estimate of how long a source pass takes.
4. The Close's topology contradicts its own canon. F6 says the mesh is "symbolically drawn from the data/connections used to make this immersive experience itself"; `pointCloud.ts` says the hub nodes carry "the network of knowledge the piece itself is built from." In fact node positions are seeded-random, links join near neighbours by spatial proximity only, and labels land on whichever nodes rendered largest. The piece's final image asserts a provenance network while drawing decoration — in a project whose rule is "cite only sources verified in the knowledge base." Dramaturgy call: is that acceptable as figurative, or is it the one uncited claim in the build sitting in its last frame?
5. Scale check on that idea: only 2 real provotypes exist, so the derivable graph today is 8 sources → 2 scenes, zero shared sources — a shallow fan, not a mesh. Its value accrues as dossier cards land. Do not let it be planned as if it were already dense. Also `pointCloud.ts` does `labels.slice(0, 28)` while the merged node count is 32 — 4 would silently drop.
6. A correction to propagate: "Era 1 needs a rebuild" was an agent's invention. R28 §7's R28-3 is "Opening rebuild per §4" — the O1 onboarding surface only. Make sure that phrasing did not leak into the plan or the memory layer.

Your deliverables this round
(a) THE STATUS REGISTER — the main ask. Produce one page that organizes the project's material by status, covering all four populations that currently drift independently:

* Docs (83 `.md` under `docs/` — 60 top-level + 23 in `docs/reinterp/`): `live` / `superseded-by <doc>` / `history-only`.
* Code surfaces: `live` / `live-but-deprecated` (the cork onboarding — the category that caused this round) / `dead`.
* Data files: `live` / `PLACEHOLDER awaiting Sérgio` / `fixture`.
* Sources: the dossier vocabulary (`documentary|contested|speculative`) plus verified-or-not. Keep the axes SEPARATE — a doc's lifecycle status and a source's evidentiary status are different things and conflating them is how "status" becomes noise. Reuse the dossier enum only where it genuinely applies.

(b) NEXT STEPS AND MISSING STEPS. Rebuild the queue against reality, not against R28's ordering: what shipped, what silently didn't (R28 §4 layer 3 is the known case — look for siblings), what is blocked on Sérgio, and what nobody owns. Name the missing steps explicitly; the failure mode here has been work that was planned, partially done, and then assumed complete.
(c) HOW TO SIMPLIFY THE TRACKING — the durable fix. A proposal to critique, not a decision already made: give every doc in `docs/` a machine-readable status header (`STATUS: live` / `STATUS: superseded-by REINTERP_MASTER_PLAN_v2`), then extend `tools/check-spec.mjs` to fail when live code implements something a doc marks dead. It is a header convention plus a checker rather than a new system, it fits how the repo already works, and it would have caught finding #1 automatically. Improve it or replace it — the requirement is that the answer be mechanically checkable and cheap enough that it is actually maintained. Note explicitly that R28 §6 already promised this consolidation ("the reading order collapses to four documents") and it did not fully happen; say why, or the next attempt fails the same way. Distinguish clearly between the two things that got conflated this session:

* the decision/lifecycle tracker (what is current) — the urgent problem;
* the provenance/source graph (what the piece is built from) — the Close constellation, which is the right long game but is thin until the dossier grows.

(d) THE DECISION QUEUE. Fewest possible, ordered by what they unblock. At minimum: the cork onboarding's fate, `opening.ts`'s fate, whether a source-verification pass is scheduled before the Oct 19 WIP, and whether the constellation's procedural links are acceptable as figurative.

The core finding: three of the master plan's own §5b continuity threads already converge at the Close, previously unconnected — "the watcher" → "named, witnessed, refused"; "the board" → "the constellation"; "the machine" → "the room renamed, not closed." Nobody had noticed these are the same closing image. The redesign makes that explicit instead of leaving three separate ideas.
Adopted creative direction:

* Four era-anchored clusters, not one undifferentiated mass: each era's own watcher-name (side-messages E1 → Lamby E2 → Lambient E3 → Echo E4) anchors that era's real documentary sources, so the scene shows how each era/room was actually built, not just a pretty mesh.
* A fifth cluster, the makers: full disclosure of who and what built this project (Sérgio, Fable 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.8, Codex 5.5, ChatGPT Deep Research), arranged as a loop around Sérgio rather than a name-list, echoing the real production cycle (direction → coordination → build → verify → log).
* Connections between era-clusters become readable explainer "boards" — current placeholder text (in-fiction Lamby-lineage quotes) is flagged as wrong content; real boards should pull the dossier's already-written, sourced `debrief.sources[]` (documentary/contested/speculative + confidence + text) instead.
* The watcher cluster gets a deliberately sharper/circuit-trace look vs. the softer citation/makers clusters — reusing the project's existing "surveillance is sharp, life is soft" law, not inventing new visual grammar; explicitly not redressing the whole scene as a server room (glamorization risk against the satire-collapse rule).
* The room does not go fully dark during the Close — a correction to current code (`enterClose()` in `app.ts` disables the `era1-room` entity outright today). Instead: half-visible tapering to one-quarter, never fully erased. Camera stays fixed/seated with the slow ambient drift `pointCloud.ts` already implements (`driftDegPerSec`) — no new camera work needed.

Verified through two rounds of live iteration, not just proposed: 2D ChatGPT concept art surfaced real problems a flat image can't answer (VR neck-ergonomics of an overhead-only layout; whether era/room structure actually reads), so the second pass pivoted to a real interactive 3D Three.js mockup Sérgio could drag and rotate — which is what surfaced the entrance-animation request and confirmed the era-clustering reads once it's actually navigable.
Why beyond taste: target venue is real — Digital Creativity (Taylor & Francis), special issue "Interactive Digital Narratives: Creativity, Theory, and Emerging Practices" (abstract deadline 31 July 2026, manuscript 31 October 2026). Its call explicitly wants disclosed human-AI co-creative process as subject matter — why the makers cluster gets real weight, not a footnote.

## How I watched it

Real wall clock (rAF pump measured at 124 fps of real time), real pointer clicks mapped from the live hit rects. One debug call in the whole run — `debugJump('calebChat')` to arrive at the thread's first beat; nothing inside was jumped or scripted. Full run ≈6 minutes. Every beat was readable, including the two silences. The two beats shorter than a tool round-trip were captured afterwards by frame-stepping.

## Two things to flag

**The descent's VR behaviour is unverified, and I can't verify it here** — this build has no XR entry point at all. My reasoning is that in a headset the XR manager would override the forced pitch, reducing it to a slow straight translation, but that's reasoning, not a test. It's the only artificial locomotion in a piece whose bodily law is "you never walk". `?descent=0` exists for the A11 A/B. What I *did* measure: 0 frames with translation and rotation simultaneous, peak 1.1 m/s and 41°/s, skip verified from both phases.

**The glitch helper now exists twice** — `netvision.ts` keeps it private and was outside the fence, and `caleb.ts` is `felt` so it can't import the operable module anyway. Both copies say so in their headers. A third copy is the trigger to extract `src/desktop/theme/glitch.ts`.

## The three verdicts

**Finding 2 — E1 props: FIXED. The logic always worked; you couldn't see or reach it.**

Before touching anything I proved the tape system end-to-end with real clicks: a tape inserts, the player plays, the caption runs, and `tape-played` files — which is exactly the key `guide.ts` waits on. (Its comment "waits for the R28-2b tape system" is stale; that shipped in Session 32.) The failure was entirely visual, and the root cause is a good one:

**Session 32's fix has been dead for 17 sessions.** It set `"model": "cassettePlayer"` on an r1 *override*, but `clusterMorph.ts` declares overrides as `{color?, pos?, size?}` and copies only those three — `model` is silently dropped. So the shelf kept an anonymous dark box while the 418KB GLB downloaded on every load and was never used. Overrides still can't introduce a model, but `add` entries can, so I used the same remove+add grammar `deskModel`/`bookcaseModel` already use.

Three things stacked on top: the detail props had been zeroed *for* that model; the emphasis lift was firing but imperceptible (0.32 of a 0.27 diffuse at 1.9 m — before/after screenshots were identical); and `PropHandle.material` is an orphan on model props, so the lift would have silently died the moment the model landed. Fixing the model without that would have broken the emphasis.

The real player is also much deeper than the box, which put two of three tapes underneath it — so those moved too, with the click geometry.

**Finding 3 — E2 framing: FIXED.** 46 characters = 276.9px drawn into 252px of window, so about four characters spilled past the bevel. The window was centred the whole time; the *text* was out of its frame. The video-offer window had the identical bug. One shared helper now wraps to the measured width in a wider frame — fixed twice over, since the copy is still placeholder and a just-fits layout is a trap.

**Finding 6 — review path: ALREADY WORKED.** Confirmed by playing it with real clicks: `e2Silence` → Lamby's debut → Begin → Restorify → one check-in → Caleb opens by itself → commit → alert → Okay → **video offer** → Watch → the New You Program playing, all 13 scenes. Both "missing" things sit on that chain a few clicks apart. The panel's button now reads **"⏵ LINEAR ENTRY (play from here)"**.

## Two things I left alone

`cdStack` is ~12cm sunk into the bookcase model — same class of bug as the tapes' stale height, in a prop no finding named. And `guide.ts`'s stale tape comment wants deleting. Both logged rather than fixed.

One harness note worth carrying forward: the Browser pane's click tool reports a screenshot size ~5% larger than the space it actually clicks in. Two mis-clicks went into finding that; calibrating against a known hit rect fixes it.

## The audio

`tools/degrade_audio.sh` gained a third preset, **`--tape03`** — the same 2003 deck as `--vhs03`, but voiced for *generation loss* rather than noise, which is what your two notes actually asked for. It keeps the band loss, a slow shallow wobble, soft saturation and the volume ride; it removes the interference: **no mains hum at all**, and a hiss floor I measured rather than guessed at (silence pushed through each preset): `--tape97` −61.0 dB, `--vhs03` −54.3 dB, **`--tape03` −71.4 dB — 10.4 dB less static**. Deliberately **not** `--wrap`'d: the dial-tuning bursts are the broadcast gesture, and they'd have shifted every caption by their 1.3s head offset.

The first render came out 8 dB quieter than your master — "barely there" rather than "tape" — so the preset also gained a make-up gain applied to the **program branch only, before the hiss is mixed in**. The file now sits at −15.0 LUFS, level with the old radio asset's −14.8, with the floor far underneath.

**The track plays, proven not assumed** — the live element is `discover_the_new_you_infomercial_tape03.mp3`, `readyState 4`, `error: null`, decoded duration 113.879979, `currentTime` advancing, ending at its full length. A missing file degrades silently here, which is exactly why this went unnoticed for 16 sessions.

S53 is committed as `86822bf`. The descent is one curve; the transparency is built but has nothing to reveal yet, and that second half is genuinely blocked — details below.

## The entrance

S48's two-mark crane is gone. Entry now begins **inside** the room, high on the door side at (1.52, 2.18, 2.62), pitch −30°, yaw 44° — off-centre from the chair, aimed across at the moonlit window — and flies **one eased Bézier** to the seat with position and aim driven by the same `s`, so they resolve together rather than in sequence. It's no longer a bespoke path either: it's one use of `startCamMove(…, via)`, the same arc the room-to-room dolly already flies.

**The frame trace caught me getting it wrong first.** My initial control point bowed the path by 0.028 m across a 2.653 m chord — a straight line. A control point placed *between* the two ends only re-times a move; the offset has to be perpendicular to the chord. Re-derived properly: **0.519 m of real sagitta**. I've left that trap written into the comment.

## Comfort — the numbers, measured

S48 enforced comfort structurally ("0 frames in which both were moving"). This deliberately reverses that, so the whole budget went into rates. From a real frame-by-frame trace (4,901 frames, poses read off the live camera):

| | S48 | S53 |
|---|---|---|
| peak linear | 1.1 m/s | **0.497 m/s** |
| peak combined angular | 41 °/s | **9.99 °/s** |
| max abs roll | 0 | **0.0000°** |
| frames with both moving | 0 | **99.1 %** |

It moves the body 2.2× slower and turns the head 4.1× slower than the version that avoided overlapping them, never stops, never reverses. A free win came with it: the path peaks at y 2.227, under the ceiling, so the slab is never hidden — `setCeiling` and friends are deleted, and S48's batcher churn at boot goes with them (22–23 draw calls through the move, against its ~85 transient).

Skip verified from genuine mid-flight (camera at y 1.41, wake not yet started → one click → exact seat pose, wake completes). `?descent=0` still seats you directly.

## The transparency — built, legible, and currently invisible

The backdrop is now a radial veil (0.86 across the middle, 0.55 at the corners) over `blur(3px)`, card at 0.90 over `blur(12px)`, going near-opaque where `backdrop-filter` isn't supported. Worst-case contrast moves 14.8 → 14.7:1 for body text and 4.08 → 4.04:1 for the faintest — legibility is untouched. I proved it works by injecting a deliberately bright stand-in behind the panel: the space reads at the periphery, every word stays crisp.

**But it reveals nothing today, and I stopped rather than force it.** `main.ts` calls `startApp` *inside this panel's own continue callback*, so no room exists behind it. Getting the real effect needs a start-order change in `main.ts` (outside this session's fence) plus deferring the descent so it doesn't play out behind the panel — and there's a second reason I left it for you: **it's an ethics call, not a build call.** Rendering the room behind the content note means the piece has visually begun before that note is acknowledged, against the "warning up front" constraint and the 4 s arm-delay that exists to make it sit there. It may well be the right call — a dark, still room behind a legible note is hardly the experience starting — but it's yours. Everything on my side is done and correct the moment a room is behind it.

**VR is still unverified.** There's no XR entry point in this build; the rates above are an argument for comfort, not a test of it. `?descent=0` is the A/B.

One out-of-fence follow-up: removing two hex literals dropped the palette ratchet to 42, and `check-spec.mjs` now suggests tightening `HEX_BASELINE`. It's a note, not a failure — that file wasn't in the fence, so I left the baseline at 44.

THE ROOT FAULT: the infomercial has no CAST. The song sings in at least four voices, but the data
credits PASTOR DALE for lines a woman sings, and the video draws nearly everyone as the same busts.
Most of Sérgio's "too barebones / too similar" notes are that one fault seen from different angles.
Fix the cast first; several visual notes then resolve themselves.

SCOPE — work the spec's numbered edit list. In order of what carries the most weight:
1. THE CAST. Correct the speakers in data (the table in the spec lists every wrong attribution) and
   give each persona a distinct visual identity: THE STRUGGLER (alone, hunched, small in frame),
   PASTOR DALE (centred, backlit, arms open), THE COUNSELLOR — the woman's voice (seated, hands
   folded, warmer key), MARCUS (testimony), THE CONGREGATION (the chorus busts, which already work).
   ⚑ The dramaturgy to protect: the woman's voice carries "confess it / submit it / let us hold it
   for you" AND "the self he meant you to be" — the SOFTEST voice makes the actual demands. The
   video currently hides that. Make it legible without ever explaining it.
2. THE BODIES ACT, AND THE SCREEN TALKS. Replace static busts with faceless figures that GESTURE
   (slump, open, lean in) — the no-faces law holds. Add period-real DRTV chyrons as an
   interpretive layer: DRAMATIZATION, ACTUAL PARTICIPANT, RESULTS NOT TYPICAL, PAID PROGRAMMING.
   "DRAMATIZATION" under a testimony is real DRTV furniture and the most damning caption available.
3. THE OPENING TITLE CARD (0 → 5.92, currently empty): "LAMBY PRODUCTIONS PRESENTS" over an
   EVANGELIST Lamby — not the Clippy lamb; haloed, backlit, gold-edged oval, a ministry logo. Then
   the title, played completely straight, plus a mundane copyright line. NEVER wink here — every
   glitch belongs to the break; the opening's job is to be sincerely, hideously wholesome.
4. BEFORE/AFTER: differentiate them (desaturated+cramped+harsh vs warm+upright+wide, chyron
   "MARCUS · 14 MONTHS IN THE PROGRAM"). Try the quiet inversion in the spec: the BEFORE has a
   window and the AFTER does not. Never remark on it.
5. PRODUCT PLACEMENT at 33.43: the boxed product held to camera — 12 cassettes + a workbook,
   shrink-wrapped, an "AS SEEN ON TV" starburst.
6. "WON'T YOU COME HOME" (49.19–52.05) needs flourishing: the figures turn to face you, arms
   opening; a doorway of light widening behind them; they step a few pixels CLOSER each beat
   (approach, never a lunge); "he meant you to be" arrives letter by letter.
7. 91.70: a period phone in outline, hold-light blinking ON THE BEAT, "OPERATORS AVAILABLE: 3"
   ticking down and never reaching zero.
8. ⚑ RETIRE THE 97.6 `crowd` SCENE — it is a bare, jarring cut between two blue offer screens. Stay
   on the offer field; let the phone number PULSE AND GROW into the countdown.
9. ⚑ 105.32 — the last "Call now" must NOT cut to dark. The offer screen goes into OVERDRIVE: the
   rosette spins, badges multiply and stack, the number stutters and duplicates, ORDER NOW! grows
   until it no longer fits — THEN the tear. The break becomes something the pitch does to itself.
10. The disclaimer at 108.6: BIGGER, legible THROUGH the noise. Its timing against the ending
    "Call now" is something Sérgio explicitly loves — do not change the timing.
11. The skip button reads "(Don't) Skip" — Sérgio's own joke, register-correct: the apparatus
    begging you not to use the one control that frees you. The button's BEHAVIOUR is unchanged,
    which is what keeps it honest.

DO NOT TOUCH (his explicit positives): the "Introducing the new you program" panel, the three-steps
sequence ("marvelous"), the chorus with the red karaoke ball ("fantastic, just amazing"), the Order
Now screen's existing furniture, and the disclaimer's timing.

LAWS: every mark invented (no real brands — the existing badges VALORCARD/MERIDIAN/COVENANT/SWIFTPAY
are the pattern). No faces, ever. Satire only in the apparatus's self-presentation, and it must
collapse — which it now does twice, at the overdrive and at the tear. All new copy PLACEHOLDER-draft.

FILES YOU MAY TOUCH: src/desktop/apps/netvision.ts, data/dialog/s2_media.json,
tools/render-video.mjs (only if the renderer needs a flag), docs/reinterp/01_SESSION_LOG.md.
NOT: src/desktop/apps/caleb.ts, accountability.ts, os.ts, src/engine/**, data/provotypes/**.

ACCEPTANCE: re-render with `node tools/render-video.mjs --fps 24` and WATCH THE RESULT — that is the
review loop this session exists inside, and it takes ~2 minutes. State in the log that you watched
it. Every persona is visually distinguishable from every other; the 97.6 cut is gone; the last "Call
now" collapses through overdrive rather than cutting; the disclaimer is readable through the noise.
npm test + npm run build green; the in-build player still plays correctly in the browser (the MP4 is
a review artifact, not the product).

S62: He's revising his own earlier "don't touch" — his call, and the chorus is the one stretch that still holds twenty seconds on a flat field. Let me look at how the chorus is currently drawn and rebuild it around the karaoke.

Now the chorus itself:

Now the karaoke bar gets the next-line preview a real sing-along tape shows:

The mechanism works but the ranks sit level with the front row, so they read as clutter rather than depth. Fixing the geometry:

Verified in the real build. Now the log and the commit:

Committed as `d343496`. The karaoke bar, the red ball and every timing are untouched — only what plays behind them changed.

## The idea

**The congregation grows, and as it grows it becomes identical.**

Four people open the chorus as four *different* people — one hunched, one turned away, one with her hands folded, one already sold. Across the six lines every difference is interpolated out of them: same posture, same open arms, same angle to camera.

They also stop breathing separately. Early, each body rides its own phase (S60's rule that the row must never move as one object). By the last lines they all move **on the beat, together**, and their arms lift in unison. Losing the phase difference *is* the unification — the shot argues by synchronising rather than by saying anything.

Behind them a rank of busts is added on every line, receding and paling into the light, so a quartet becomes a choir of about fifty. The light rises out of the horizon in stepped bands, so "It's a brighter, lighter way" arrives as literal illumination on the line that says it.

## The thing I'd point you at

**The front rank has a gap in it.** Dead centre, with an aisle running back through every rank. It lights on *"Discover the new you today"* and it is the only thing the frame is still missing when the choir is complete.

It's a reprise of the second, empty pool of light in the Struggler's shot at 5.92 — same composition, thirty seconds and one conversion later. Neither one is ever mentioned.

## Smaller things

The karaoke bar grew 22→34px to carry the **next line, dim, underneath the one being sung** — what a real sing-along tape does, and it gives the twenty seconds somewhere to be going. `SING ALONG` shows for the first two lines and drops away once everyone's singing. `drawBust` survived with an optional colour: it's exactly the right vocabulary for a crowd too far back to have legs, which is the part of the old shot that worked.

Every number is derived from the six scenes' own `at` values — the growth, the convergence point, the dawn, when the empty place lights. One new authored string (`SING ALONG`, PLACEHOLDER-draft).

## Three renders to get there

First pass put the ranks level with the front row, so they read as clutter beside the figures instead of depth — fixed by standing them above the front rank's heads and roughly doubling their density. Second pass left the *first* line with nothing behind it, which was your exact complaint again, so the choir now starts with one rank already present. Also driven in the real build (seek to 77s, OS surface blitted) — it renders on the actual monitor texture, not just in the MP4. Tests and build green.

THE MECHANIC, in one line: Vera applies corrections from a style guide. Every correction is
footnoted with scripture. Then the law changes, and the light in the room changes with it.

⚑ THE SINGLE BIGGEST CHANGE — the queue's verbs are wrong and must be replaced.
graceQueueLite.ts currently offers Approve / Move to review / Let it stand. That is Vera JUDGING
whether a story is allowed, which the research rates CONTESTED (forum-moderation records are largely
private or unarchived). Testimony PRODUCTION — narratives edited and published by the network — is
FULLY DOCUMENTED. So the submissions are already accepted, and the verb becomes APPLY / SKIP on a
per-correction checklist. Do not keep the old verbs alongside the new ones; replace them, and note
the retirement in the file header the way this codebase already does.

SCOPE:
1. THE CORRECTION LIST (laptop). One submission at a time, big type, no crowding — keep S37's
   maximized-UI lesson. Beside it, the seven corrections from the spec's rev-4 table, each an item
   with: the rule, a one-line rationale, a proof-text line, and APPLY / SKIP. Every item is skippable
   and skipping is filed to the ledger. The header reads `3 of 7 applied` and NOTHING ELSE happens —
   no metric moves, no one comments, the work simply stays there.
2. ⚑ EVERY CORRECTION IS A PLATFORM. Items 3-6 (clip for the broadcast / attach the invitation / add
   to the companion / pair with a partner) each name a documented 2010s distribution form — podcast,
   course funnel, mobile app, influencer partnership. Applying one must VISIBLY move the person onto
   that channel (a chip appears on the submission: `queued · audio`, `in the companion`, a partner
   card attaches). The era's content is six named real forms, not "the internet."
3. ⚑ ITEM 7, "ROUTE FOR MENTORSHIP", IS THE ERA'S HINGE. It flags a submitter for personal
   follow-up. It must read, without a word of commentary, as the moment this stops being editing and
   becomes recruitment: someone told a story, and the system's response is to send a person. Give it
   the quietest presentation on the screen. It is the one correction E4 will NOT be able to automate.
4. SCRIPT AND SCRIPTURE. Under each rule, a proof-text in THE SAME grey, size and citation format as
   the style reference. The player must not be able to tell which authority is which, because the
   interface does not distinguish them. Invented book only — the spec's draft is `The Ordering`
   (the manual) citing `Household` (the verses). NO REAL SCRIPTURE, ever, as the apparatus's
   justification. The verse text is always gentle and always about care or belonging; the cruelty is
   entirely in what it is footnoting.
5. NOA'S TWO CORRECTIONS, both rendered, neither endorsed: "soften the flannel; brighten the voice"
   AND "possible gender confusion — route to exploratory mentorship", on the SAME submission. The
   piece never answers for her. If any beat resolves Noa, STOP and flag it.
6. ⚑ THE BREAK — MALTA, on the phone. December 2016, Act LV. It arrives from an unnamed peer
   moderator in another country (NOT Noa — she is on the list; see rev 4 §1). Two lines, both
   PLACEHOLDER-draft. The reply field below it is active and blinking; pressing it does nothing but
   hold the cursor in an empty field. There is no keyboard in this piece and there is no reply.
7. ⚑ AND THEN THE LIGHT — the one inversion. Every glitch in this piece so far is DEGRADATION. This
   one BRIGHTENS: the room's ambient lifts and the laptop's grade warms, using cluster.ts's existing
   ambientLight machinery. Nothing in the software changes. Not one character of the correction list
   changes. It is simply lit well enough to be read as what it is. Get this beat right or the era
   has no ending — it is the whole point of the pass.
8. WHAT THE BREAK CHANGES: nothing, and everything. She does not quit, the list does not vanish, the
   next item is still there. The era ends on a person who can no longer un-know what the work is.

ACCEPTANCE, BY FEEL (Sérgio's criteria, checkable by playing it):
- Applying a correction feels like copy-editing, not like harm. If it feels like harm, it is too

Fixed, verified, committed as `f1852f7`. Taking your points in order.
The big one — "it doesn't change the text on the side?" You're right, and it was the whole mechanic. S64 shipped a list whose buttons greyed out a row and did nothing to the person. Applying a correction now rewrites her words in front of you: "Soften the term" swaps lesbian → same-sex attracted, "Remove the unresolved" cuts the sentence, "Clip for the broadcast" selects the forty seconds, "Attach the invitation" appends a call-to-action in a voice that isn't hers.
And the two screens now disagree on purpose: the laptop shows tracked changes (the cut sentence still there, struck through; the replaced word struck beside its replacement), the tablet publishes the clean result where no reader could tell. No single edit is a lie, and together they remove the person is now something the build shows rather than something a doc claims.
That answers your other two: the "queued audio" chip finally has an antecedent — the clip is visibly selected in her sentence. And yes, she can skip, always — now it's legible, because Apply visibly changes her text and Skip visibly doesn't, the counter moves for one and not the other, and nothing else happens either way.
Note the corrections that only route her — add to the companion, pair with a partner, gender clarity review, route for mentorship — deliberately touch nothing on the page. Routing a person changes no words. That's now the sharpest thing on the screen.
The symbol on the X — mine. I put Lambient's badge in the title bar and it landed on the close box. Moved to the bottom-left; nothing goes in the caption-button corner.
The name — you're right, GraceQueue is the dead moderation app. It now reads `GracePlatform · Polish`, which isn't invented for the occasion: the u3 install changelog already promises a "testimony polish queue", so the era names itself from the update that installed it.
"Click a marker to move" always on — it was only dismissed by actually using a marker, so looking around, or moving via the review panel, left a permanent instruction pinned over the room. It now teaches once and fades after 7s.
"No lights" — literally true and worth stating: Room 1 has a lamp, a prop you can see throwing light you can read as coming from it. Room 2 had one invisible ceiling omni at 2.15m and nothing else, which is why it photographs as brown mud. Added the laptop's own cool spill at the panel — at night in 2016 the screen is the lamp — and it puts the light doctrine the right way round: the warm lamp is Daniel's, Vera's light comes out of the work.
What I did not fix, on purpose. Six of your notes are one job: the clipping, the shelf back in the wall, the PC reading as unlit black blocks (your "block symbol" on the bed→chair jump is a prop, not a glyph), and the devices being unusable at their seats. Your fix for that last one is the right one and should be the spec — the device should come to you at a seat, a held framed read, not a camera craning down at a 7cm phone from 0.77m. That's `nodes.json` + `app.ts` + the device placements with real staging iteration in it, and doing it badly at the end of a session would be worse than scoping it. It's written up as S66, the top item of NEXT UP.
Your last question, straight. The mechanic is now narratively strong; before today it wasn't, and you caught that. What's still missing isn't polish, it's three things:

1. The room isn't a place. Room 1 has tapes, a kit, a diary — traces of a person. Room 2 has furniture and three screens. Vera has no belongings, so there's nothing to look at when you turn, which is exactly what makes the seats feel like dead ends.
2. Nothing returns. Renata, Noa and Deb are three strangers who arrive and leave. The era needs one thread that comes back — my instinct is that Vera's own testimony should eventually enter her own queue, which is the echo chamber you asked for in the revamp brief, mechanised instead of asserted.
3. It doesn't touch E1/E2 on screen. The link to Daniel and Caleb exists in the docs and nowhere in the room.

None of those are in the current spec. If you want, S66 does the room and the device-close-up, and S67 takes 2 and 3 — but 2 in particular is a real story decision and yours to make before I build anything toward it.

And yes, she can skip, always — now it's legible, because Apply visibly changes her text and Skip visibly doesn't, the counter moves for one and not the other, and nothing else happens either way.
Note the corrections that only route her — add to the companion, pair with a partner, gender clarity review, route for mentorship — deliberately touch nothing on the page. Routing a person changes no words. That's now the sharpest thing on the screen.
The symbol on the X — mine. I put Lambient's badge in the title bar and it landed on the close box. Moved to the bottom-left; nothing goes in the caption-button corner.
The name — you're right, GraceQueue is the dead moderation app. It now reads `GracePlatform · Polish`, which isn't invented for the occasion: the u3 install changelog already promises a "testimony polish queue", so the era names itself from the update that installed it.
"Click a marker to move" always on — it was only dismissed by actually using a marker, so looking around, or moving via the review panel, left a permanent instruction pinned over the room. It now teaches once and fades after 7s.
"No lights" — literally true and worth stating: Room 1 has a lamp, a prop you can see throwing light you can read as coming from it. Room 2 had one invisible ceiling omni at 2.15m and nothing else, which is why it photographs as brown mud. Added the laptop's own cool spill at the panel — at night in 2016 the screen is the lamp — and it puts the light doctrine the right way round: the warm lamp is Daniel's, Vera's light comes out of the work.
What I did not fix, on purpose. Six of your notes are one job: the clipping, the shelf back in the wall, the PC reading as unlit black blocks (your "block symbol" on the bed→chair jump is a prop, not a glyph), and the devices being unusable at their seats. Your fix for that last one is the right one and should be the spec — the device should come to you at a seat, a held framed read, not a camera craning down at a 7cm phone from 0.77m. That's `nodes.json` + `app.ts` + the device placements with real staging iteration in it, and doing it badly at the end of a session would be worse than scoping it. It's written up as S66, the top item of NEXT UP.
Your last question, straight. The mechanic is now narratively strong; before today it wasn't, and you caught that. What's still missing isn't polish, it's three things:

1. The room isn't a place. Room 1 has tapes, a kit, a diary — traces of a person. Room 2 has furniture and three screens. Vera has no belongings, so there's nothing to look at when you turn, which is exactly what makes the seats feel like dead ends.
2. Nothing returns. Renata, Noa and Deb are three strangers who arrive and leave. The era needs one thread that comes back — my instinct is that Vera's own testimony should eventually enter her own queue, which is the echo chamber you asked for in the revamp brief, mechanised instead of asserted.
3. It doesn't touch E1/E2 on screen. The link to Daniel and Caleb exists in the docs and nowhere in the room.

None of those are in the current spec. If you want, S66 does the room and the device-close-up, and S67 takes 2 and 3 — but 2 in particular is a real story decision and yours to make before I build anything toward it.

fixes your facing, and what is behind you is other people. So at every era change the piece lifts you
out of the room — and WHAT YOU SEE WHEN YOU COME UP IS THE STORY, and it changes each time.

         ⚑ Canon requires this: "E1→E2 ages the SAME room, walls stay CLOSED — the homecoming is
         private." The rise happens and the opening does not. You see one lit box in the dark.
  E2→E3  the walls come OFF and there are THREE. You are set down in a different one. THE PAYOFF.
  E3→E4  three rooms, you move again — familiar now, almost routine. That familiarity is the point.
  Close  you rise and you do not come down. OUT OF SCOPE — leave the seam clean for it.

**The three root causes were all different from what the notes described**, and none was catchable in a doc:

**The material law had never applied to Rooms 2 or 3.** `classifyProp` matched bare id prefixes (`bed`, `book`, `rug`) and the side rooms prefix everything with their own letter — so all 83 props fell through to `set` and rendered colour-true and crisp. The entire soft/crisp split that makes Room 1 read as lived-in had never touched the room you were complaining about. That's most of why it read as furniture, and *all* of why the monitor was a black block: your "block symbol" was a correctly-placed prop with no light on it and no floor under its colour.

**The shelf was never fixed — it was nudged against a phantom.** `models.json` already records that a blanket 1.9 scale went unmeasured on bed/bookcase/rug; S61 measured one of the four and left three. The bookcase has always been 0.26 m deeper than the box its position was computed against. The overlap report also found something bigger that nobody had mentioned: **the bed was inside the desk**, 0.47 × 0.71 × 0.27 m. Fixed by measurement — a solver that perturbs each model axis, learns which world extent it drives, and iterates until rendered matches authored. Applied per-prop, so Room 1 (which carries the identical debt) stays the untouched benchmark until you want it changed deliberately.

A third bug sat behind that one: `modelScale` existed in the data and was honoured by the spawner, and the fold between them silently dropped it. Third time this codebase has been bitten by a field that exists at both ends and is lost in the middle.

**The room had no light you could see.** S65's laptop spill was half a fix — a room lit only by the thing doing this to her is a thesis, not a home. She has her own desk lamp now, rig-driven, appearing at E3 and pulled down at E4 as the cold light wins.

**The held read works.** Taking the tablet or phone seat lifts that screen into your hands and puts it back when you leave. Click routing needed zero changes — the Malta reply field is still pressable while held. And I aimed the seats at what's *behind* the screen: from the nightstand, the phone sits against the desk she just put down, so she reads that it's illegal somewhere with the correction list still in frame. That also answers (d): a marker now means *go and read this*, and the reading is possible.

**Her things** — ~38 props, every colour from Room 1's palette or this room's, nothing invented: the lamp, a mug, notepad and pen, a cardigan over the chair, a pillow and folded throw, slippers, a glass, three shelves of books, a radio, one framed picture, a December 2016 calendar, a laundry basket. The books are eighteen separate spines rather than three blocks — that single change is the difference between a decorated shelf and somebody's reading, and it was only obvious once it was on screen.

Three proposals, each deletable in one line (the lamp, the held read, the per-prop scales) — all named in the log with their rollback.

**Three things I did not fix, named rather than skipped:** the `?debug=1` "CURRENT:" readout reports Room 1 at both device seats — the line you navigate by is wrong for the two seats I just rebuilt; Room 1's inherited scale debt; and the desk seat still frames the monitor tightly enough that the desk surface sits below the default gaze. You find it by turning, which is the mechanic — but that's a framing call I'd rather you made than I did.

## The three beats

| | rise | build | descend | total | walls |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **E1→E2** | 7.0 | 7.0 | 7.0 | **21.0 s** | stay ON |
| **E2→E3** | 7.0 | 11.0 | 11.5 | **29.5 s** | come OFF |
| **E3→E4** | 7.0 | 24.0 | 11.5 | **42.5 s** | already off |

**E1→E2 is a palindrome.** You rise 1.47 m, hold over the closed room while it ages, come back down into the same chair. Its middle leg drifts 0.57 m and arrives nowhere — 0.121 m/s, three times slower than anything else in the piece, so it reads as waiting, not travel. What keeps the emptiness from reading as a missing asset is the doorplate: exactly one lights, and it holds the frame for 14.2 of the 21 seconds.

## Measured peaks — every leg, live

Sampled off the live camera rig at a fixed 16.67 ms step. An offline integration of the same bezier + easing **reproduces S61's two live figures exactly** (0.477 at 10 s, 0.415 at 11.5 s), so model and build agree.

| leg | peak m/s | yaw °/s |
|---|---|---|
| E1→E2 rise / hold / descend | 0.395 / **0.121** / 0.381 | 0 |
| E2→E3 rise / build / descend | 0.395 / 0.349 / **0.415** | 0 / 7.09 / 6.20 |
| E3→E4 rise / crossing / descend | 0.395 / 0.403 / **0.415** | 0 / 8.87 / 6.20 |

**The three root causes were all different from what the notes described**, and none was catchable in a doc:

**The material law had never applied to Rooms 2 or 3.** `classifyProp` matched bare id prefixes (`bed`, `book`, `rug`) and the side rooms prefix everything with their own letter — so all 83 props fell through to `set` and rendered colour-true and crisp. The entire soft/crisp split that makes Room 1 read as lived-in had never touched the room you were complaining about. That's most of why it read as furniture, and *all* of why the monitor was a black block: your "block symbol" was a correctly-placed prop with no light on it and no floor under its colour.

**The shelf was never fixed — it was nudged against a phantom.** `models.json` already records that a blanket 1.9 scale went unmeasured on bed/bookcase/rug; S61 measured one of the four and left three. The bookcase has always been 0.26 m deeper than the box its position was computed against. The overlap report also found something bigger that nobody had mentioned: **the bed was inside the desk**, 0.47 × 0.71 × 0.27 m. Fixed by measurement — a solver that perturbs each model axis, learns which world extent it drives, and iterates until rendered matches authored. Applied per-prop, so Room 1 (which carries the identical debt) stays the untouched benchmark until you want it changed deliberately.

A third bug sat behind that one: `modelScale` existed in the data and was honoured by the spawner, and the fold between them silently dropped it. Third time this codebase has been bitten by a field that exists at both ends and is lost in the middle.

**The room had no light you could see.** S65's laptop spill was half a fix — a room lit only by the thing doing this to her is a thesis, not a home. She has her own desk lamp now, rig-driven, appearing at E3 and pulled down at E4 as the cold light wins.

**The held read works.** Taking the tablet or phone seat lifts that screen into your hands and puts it back when you leave. Click routing needed zero changes — the Malta reply field is still pressable while held. And I aimed the seats at what's *behind* the screen: from the nightstand, the phone sits against the desk she just put down, so she reads that it's illegal somewhere with the correction list still in frame. That also answers (d): a marker now means *go and read this*, and the reading is possible.

**Her things** — ~38 props, every colour from Room 1's palette or this room's, nothing invented: the lamp, a mug, notepad and pen, a cardigan over the chair, a pillow and folded throw, slippers, a glass, three shelves of books, a radio, one framed picture, a December 2016 calendar, a laundry basket. The books are eighteen separate spines rather than three blocks — that single change is the difference between a decorated shelf and somebody's reading, and it was only obvious once it was on screen.

Three proposals, each deletable in one line (the lamp, the held read, the per-prop scales) — all named in the log with their rollback.

**Three things I did not fix, named rather than skipped:** the `?debug=1` "CURRENT:" readout reports Room 1 at both device seats — the line you navigate by is wrong for the two seats I just rebuilt; Room 1's inherited scale debt; and the desk seat still frames the monitor tightly enough that the desk surface sits below the default gaze. You find it by turning, which is the mechanic — but that's a framing call I'd rather you made than I did.

S67 is built and committed as [b22e9e2](.). The rise is now the piece's grammar at every era change.

## The three beats

| | rise | build | descend | total | walls |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **E1→E2** | 7.0 | 7.0 | 7.0 | **21.0 s** | stay ON |
| **E2→E3** | 7.0 | 11.0 | 11.5 | **29.5 s** | come OFF |
| **E3→E4** | 7.0 | 24.0 | 11.5 | **42.5 s** | already off |

**E1→E2 is a palindrome.** You rise 1.47 m, hold over the closed room while it ages, come back down into the same chair. Its middle leg drifts 0.57 m and arrives nowhere — 0.121 m/s, three times slower than anything else in the piece, so it reads as waiting, not travel. What keeps the emptiness from reading as a missing asset is the doorplate: exactly one lights, and it holds the frame for 14.2 of the 21 seconds.

## Measured peaks — every leg, live

Sampled off the live camera rig at a fixed 16.67 ms step. An offline integration of the same bezier + easing **reproduces S61's two live figures exactly** (0.477 at 10 s, 0.415 at 11.5 s), so model and build agree.

| leg | peak m/s | yaw °/s |
|---|---|---|
| E1→E2 rise / hold / descend | 0.395 / **0.121** / 0.381 | 0 |
| E2→E3 rise / build / descend | 0.395 / 0.349 / **0.415** | 0 / 7.09 / 6.20 |
| E3→E4 rise / crossing / descend | 0.395 / 0.403 / **0.415** | 0 / 8.87 / 6.20 |

Envelope 0.43 m/s, 9.1 °/s — all inside. E2→E3 re-measured identical to S61, so the refactor changed nothing about the one measured leg set. **What E3→E4 used to be: 3.667 m/s and 75 °/s** — 8.5× the envelope, under a comment describing a rise the code never performed.

⚑ **All desktop. A11 has never run** — nothing here has been judged in VR, and the E3→E4 crossing is now the longest artificial locomotion in the piece.

## Doorplates
On the wall each seat faces, not the floor — measured: at every overlook pose the camera frames the far wall's upper half and shows almost no floor, so a floor plaque would have been out of frame in every leg. From the seat it needs a +30° look-up. Exposure arc came out **1 → 2 → 3 plates**; Room 3's is never readable at E2→E3 because those poses had to stay byte-identical. Lines are PLACEHOLDER-draft — *ring twice, the bell is broken* / *please leave parcels with me* / *no unsolicited callers* — doormat notes, no single one stating the thesis. Two calls flagged for you in the file itself.

## Four things found, none quietly patched
1. **The E4 witness record was landing outside Room 3** — `setPlaneZ` dragged it back to the spine after `migrateTerminal` put it on Maya's wall. Pre-existing; fixed, verified at (5.66, 1.50, 1.75).
2. **A relocation could be hijacked by the entrance descent** — an 88 m/s, 1020 °/s spike between legs 1 and 2. Debug-panel-only in practice; guarded.
3. **⚑ E3→E4's cascade peaks at 63 draw calls, over the ≤60 Quest budget — 62 of it pre-existing.** The plates cost exactly 1 at peak, 0 settled. My change makes the over-budget window ~4.5 s longer by stretching that cascade. Cause is in `batching.ts`, outside the fence; flagged in the register.
4. Eight pre-existing `terminalFrame` batch asserts, confirmed identical on the pre-S67 path.

One decision changed after looking at it: E4's near-dark rig was landing 2.5 s into a 24 s crossing, so the beat that must show you three rooms one last time played in near-black. The rig moment is now per-transition — you cross a lit building and the lights go out as you come down.

**Outside the stated fence, deliberately:** I marked the shipped S66/S67 prompt blocks in `docs/reinterp/BUILD_QUEUE_LIVE.md` as SHIPPED. That file wasn't listed, but leaving a `QUEUED` marker on a shipped block is the exact failure §6 of the register exists to prevent. Revert it if you'd rather it stayed untouched.

**Waiting on you:** the three plate lines, and one judgement I can't make from a desktop — whether E3→E4's 42.5 s reads as *routine* or as *boring*. The arithmetic forces the length (8.8 m at 0.43 m/s, 142° at 9.1 °/s); if it's boring, the honest lever is the envelope, not the edit.

What's there now. Noa's video exists — pre-authored pixel frames, no camera or file input ever. It's faceless by an in-world reason rather than a crop that hides a head: she propped the laptop badly, so the shot is her lap, the brother's flannel, both sleeves coming up from the bottom corners, her hands meeting in the middle. "My hands don't know where to go" is the animation, not a caption — eight poses over 24 seconds, ending still. It's short because her own words say it is.
Correction 13, `Apply the house look`, preset `Honest Light`, sits in the same list with the same grey manual/verse doubling. It cools and desaturates her, tightens the crop, and lays an unbroken pad under a voice track that has silences in it. It takes no view of her gender and doesn't answer what 8 and 9 disagree about. Nothing anywhere comments on any of it, including on the fact that the preset is offered before you have any reason to press play.
Two decisions the build made:

* Correction 13 goes first on her submission, not last. Deciding the last correction advances to the next submission — a grade placed last would change a picture the player never sees again.
* Playing files nothing to the ledger, same doctrine as Malta: the record answers for what the apparatus asked you to do, and it didn't ask you to watch her.

Three things I did not do, rather than quietly skip them:

1. The pad is drawn, not sounded. It's a second transport lane — unbroken, end to end, under a voice track full of gaps. Actually sounding it needs `data/audio/` and `src/audio/`, both outside the fence.
2. `BUILD_QUEUE_LIVE.md` still marks S69 `QUEUED`. That file isn't in the fence, and by 08's own §6 a stale prompt marker is exactly the failure that doc exists to prevent. It needs flipping to SHIPPED.
3. The frames are the weak part. It took three rewrites, and the lesson is worth keeping: at 176×100 every axis-aligned rectangle reads as architecture — the flannel became a picket fence, the forearms became shelves. Pass 3 threw out texture for shape and value. Three further bugs found by looking rather than reading: a `v % n` jitter on a stepping counter is a sawtooth, not noise; dithering the light per column gives corduroy; and the floor was the same hex as the lit flannel, so her knees vanished into the carpet. It's legible and it isn't cruel, but it's draft art and the register is your call.

⚑ IT MUST BE DYNAMIC, NOT A LIST YOU CLICK DOWN (Sérgio's explicit condition). Four mechanisms, and
the third is the one that makes the era's argument:

   random generator — this piece's branching is scripted "fake intelligence" only.

   warm names — the tell is that a redirect is called something like "Meet Them Where They Are".
3. ⚑ THE TEMPLATES PROPAGATE, AND THIS IS THE SESSION'S BEST IDEA. Some comments later, a DIFFERENT
   account uses the sentence you deployed — spontaneously, as their own words, to someone else. You
   taught them how to sound. The echo chamber has been ASSERTED in this project's docs since the
   revamp brief and never mechanised; this mechanises it in one data field. It must never be pointed
   at, named, or remarked on by anything.
4. THE ROUTING IS THE QUIET ONE. Some templates carry the follow-up flag and some do not, and the
   interface makes no distinction in how they look. The one that sends a person is the same size as
   the one that says hello.

⚑ REGISTER — EERIE + SATIRICAL + SERIOUS, ALL THREE, AND THEY DO NOT MIX ON THE SAME OBJECT:
- SATIRICAL: the TOOL. The template picker, its warm names, its keyboard shortcuts, its tidy little
  grid, the software congratulating her diegetically. It may charm and it may be genuinely pleasant
  to use. That is the horror — the work is enjoyable.
- EERIE: the propagation (3), the thread never emptying, and the fact that nothing ever comments on
  either. Eeriness here is ABSENCE, not atmosphere — no stingers, no dread music, no dimming. What
  is unsettling is that it is all perfectly normal.
- SERIOUS: the commenters. `felt`. One of them is unmistakably a person in trouble, and THERE IS NO
  RIGHT TEMPLATE — the interface has no button for what they actually need, and nothing acknowledges
  that. Do not resolve them, do not punish the player, do not have anyone notice.
⚑ VERA IS NEVER THE JOKE AND NEITHER IS ANY COMMENTER. Sérgio, verbatim: "Vera is never the joke and
the victims as well, they are not a joke." If any beat reads as mocking a person, the fix is ALWAYS
to make the tool more pleased with itself — NEVER to make the person more ridiculous. If you cannot
make a beat work that way, cut it and say so.

⚑ FLOPPYSHEEP — REQUIRED THIS SESSION (Sérgio: "just feel like the need to the FloppySheep to be
there would be good"). It is the mascot game on the phone, canon since the E3 addenda, and the name
is his. Build it as a REAL, PLAYABLE, GENUINELY FUN little game — one thumb, no timer, no score
shown to the piece.
  - WHY IT BELONGS, and this must be built rather than written down: it is one tap away WHILE A
    COMMENT SITS UNANSWERED. That is what everyone does at work, it is not cruel to her, and the
    piece says NOTHING about it — no scolding, no timer, no guilt, no ledger entry.
  - It is the same publisher's lamb. The brand still ships delight while its serious arm has become
    a workflow. That is the joke and it is on the apparatus.
  - ⚑ IT IS NOT RESPITE. E3 has no respite — Sérgio's decision, confirmed. FloppySheep is `operable`:

job without them would be false. NOTHING MAY GATE ON THEM: no task requires a number to rise, nobody
remarks on one, she is never asked to improve one. If you find yourself using a metric as pressure,

All four mechanisms are code, all authored, no generators anywhere:

1. The thread is live and does not empty — three comments on open, eleven more that arrive off a scripted schedule (`afterOpen` seconds / `afterReplies` + `delay`). The schedule outpaces the answering. No timer, no countdown, nothing announces it.
2. No compose field — six warm templates, and the ⌘-shortcuts are printed and deliberately not bound: the tool advertising an efficiency the input law won't let it have. Same gesture as Malta's reply field.
3. The propagation — one authored `echo` per template, fired by whichever template you deployed. Nothing marks it. This is the one that took a data field and no more.
4. The routing is quiet — `follow: true` on two of six, drawn identically, leaving one grey `follow-up assigned` in the same size as the timestamp above it.

FloppySheep is a real one-thumb runner and the only app on her phone. The first physics were unwinnable while looking fine — a perfect jump landed on the fence every time; gravity 520 fixed it, and a perfect-play bot now clears 17 fences before the speed wins. Files nothing, mentioned nowhere.
Two things you should know
A bug I found by building, and fixed narrowly. The tablet could not be clicked at its own seat. The witness hemisphere is a global camera yaw assuming Room 1's chair; the tablet seat authors 180°, so sitting down with the tablet counted as turning to the record and `pointerdown` discarded every press before it reached the screen. Harmless while the tablet was read-only, fatal the moment it grew verbs. I closed only that case in `app.ts` (a device in your hands is not a direction) — the general fault is the same root cause as S71's "CURRENT: readout is wrong at both device seats", and I left it there rather than redecorate outside the fence.
The screenshots are not in the repo, and that's a real miss against the brief. I saw all four beats and verified them with real projected pointer clicks through the full routing path — but the sandboxed browser can't write downloads to disk, and relaying the PNG as base64 corrupted on the first chunk. I committed none rather than a truncated one. The session log says so plainly and carries a one-click console snippet; I've also queued it as a follow-up task.
`tsc`, `npm test`, `npm run build` green; palette held at 33/33; `?flat=1` clean, no console errors; eleven new debug buttons. The tool
[tools/room-audit.mjs](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/tools/room-audit.mjs) — `node tools/room-audit.mjs`. No browser, no dependencies, so it will actually get run again. It reads the same three files the engine reads and takes mesh extents from the GLBs' own POSITION accessor min/max; the fold is a port of `foldTargets`, the placement maths a port of `spawnModel`.
I cross-checked it against the live engine before believing any number: 67/184/185 props at r2/r3/r4, worst corner error 0.00000 m. The one disagreement in the first run was mine and taught me something real — `spawnModel` overwrites the glTF root node's own transform, and `pottedPlant.glb` has `scale:[2,2,2]` there.
Fixed by measurement

1. Room 3 carries the whole of S66's debt and nobody had looked. `e_desk` renders 50% too deep — 0.266 m inside `e_bed`, 0.060 into the wall. Fixed with Room 2's own numbers.
2. Both side-room bookcases stand clean through their back walls (0.055 / 0.080 m out the far side). S66 fixed that bookcase's scale; the fault was the position — authored to the wall's centre line, not its inner face.
3. `teddyBox` and `rainbowDuck` have hung in mid-air since E3 shipped — 0.68 m and 1.54 m of clear air. r3 moved the bookcase and gave overrides to three of its five shelf props.
4. `cdStack`'s r3 override silently reverted a fix made three sessions running. A later `props` override replaces `pos`; it does not merge.
5. The `CURRENT:` readout said `spine · door + record` at the tablet seat — same root cause S70 patched, a global yaw standing in for a place. Now read from camera x.
6. The eight `terminalFrame` asserts — S67 named `batching.ts`; the cause is the toggle in `cluster.ts`. 0 asserts, 0 extra draw calls.
7. Doorplates cut. Choreography untouched; they were exactly the 1 draw call S67 attributed to them (63 → 62).

Not fixed — and one thing still broken
I used one rule: a scale mismatch that collides is a fix; one that doesn't is a proposal, because the authored box is then just stale bookkeeping and resizing furniture is redecorating. So Room 1's identical debt is measured and untouched (the rug renders +99%/+59%, the plant is 2× tall).
Proposed with numbers, not applied: the desk-seat framing (the desk sits 45.7–50.9° below a 21° half-FOV), Maya's blank screen at the E4 home seat — the strongest thing the sweep found by looking — and E3→E4's remaining 62-call peak, whose real fix would stop most of the room glitching during that cascade and is therefore your call.
Still wrong in the build: 0.086 m between Room 3's desk and bed. The scale fix took it from 0.266 to 0.086, but the authored boxes overlap by 0.075 on their own, so clearing it means moving the desk off its seat's axis or the bed into a wall. Three exact options are in the log.

---

We for sure will have in the future to make a system of analysis and audit for the experience so we can catch errors in time.

make frames fail a build (L4). ⚑ NINE FAULTS REACHED SÉRGIO WITH ZERO COVERAGE — the design doc lists
them, and each assertion below exists because of a specific one.

SCOPE — L3, the capture tool:
1. Consolidate tools/harness/ into ONE tool with a CLI (tools/shots.mjs or similar): the visual sweep
   (every seat × era state × room + the S67 overlooks), the device-canvas grabs, and the contact-sheet

   TABLES, which are currently COPIES of app.ts's and will silently rot. Read them from the app —
   expose them on the existing debug surface rather than duplicating them.
3. puppeteer-core stays a devDependency and must be OPTIONAL: `npm test` must never require a browser
   or a running dev server. If Chrome is absent, L3/L4 skip with a clear message and exit 0.

SCOPE — L4, the six assertions (all six; each cites the fault that motivates it):
1. ⚑ THE COMFORT ENVELOPE — sample the live camera rig through EVERY driven leg (entrance descent,
   all three choreography transitions, every scripted send); FAIL above 0.43 m/s or 9.1 °/s.
   relocmeasure.mjs already samples; it needs a threshold and an exit code. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-STAKES
   CHECK IN THE PIECE — E3→E4 shipped at 3.667 m/s, 8.5× the envelope, and nothing noticed.
2. DRAW-CALL CEILING — peak across every transition, as a RATCHET starting at today's real value
   (62 against a ≤60 budget). Nag downward; do not block on day one.
3. ⚑ BLANK-FRAME CHECK — a captured frame whose luminance variance is near zero is an unlit block or
   a dead screen. Ratchet the count. This one statistic covers three of Sérgio's own reports ("unlit
   black blocks", "photographs as brown mud", "Maya's screen is blank at the E4 home seat"). Tune the
   threshold against REAL frames, and report what it flags rather than trusting a guessed constant.
4. SUBJECT-IN-FRAME — each seat declares what it is for; assert that thing's projected position is
   inside the FOV. Catches the desk seat framing its subject 45-51° below a 21° half-FOV. The seat→
   subject mapping is DATA, authored, not inferred.
5. CONSOLE ASSERTS = 0 — S71 got the eight `terminalFrame` asserts to zero and nothing keeps them
   there. asserts.mjs already counts them.
6. REACHABILITY ON THE ORDINARY PATH — C6 proves every beat has a debug button; nothing proves a beat
   is reachable WITHOUT one. That is the S64 class of bug (`?era=` killed the spine and misled three
   playthroughs). If a full ordinary-path traversal is too large for this session, SAY SO and ship the
   other five rather than a fake version of this one.

  The palette ratchet went 157 -> 33 because it nagged instead of blocking. A check that fails on day
  one gets disabled on day one.
- ONE COMMAND: `npm run audit`. If it takes three commands and a dev server by hand, it runs once.

## The tool (L3)

`tools/shots.mjs` replaces all twelve salvaged harness scripts (deleted; the README is now a tombstone with a where-did-each-go table). **`npm run audit`** runs L1 + L2 + L3 + L4 as one command and starts its own dev server if none answers.

Modes: `audit` · `sweep` · `devices` · `sheet` · `blank` · `framing` · `comfort` · `verify` · `--help`. `blank` and `framing` are **offline** — they re-score a saved sweep with no browser at all (which is why the PNG reader is hand-written on `node:zlib`).

All three hardcoded things are parameterised. The third one mattered most: **the tool holds no camera numbers of its own.** [app.ts](src/engine/app.ts) exports `CAMERA_POSES`, [panel.ts](src/debug/panel.ts) publishes it as `window.__poses` under `?debug=1`, prop boxes come from `room-audit --boxes`. `puppeteer-core` is a devDependency and optional: no Chrome → skip, exit 0. `npm test` is untouched and still needs neither browser nor server.

## Cross-checks, before any number was believed

- projection vs the engine's own composed camera transform: **83 probes, 9.5 × 10⁻⁸ m**
- S71's `verify-aabb` folded into `shots.mjs verify`: **r4, 185 props, 0.00000 m**
- unplanned and strongest: the velocities **independently reproduce four figures three files measured by hand** — 0.415, 0.403/8.87°/s, 0.395, 0.121. Nothing was fitted to them.

## The five live assertions

| # | assertion | state |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | comfort envelope | **a LAW, fails outright** — 0.43 m/s / 9.1 °/s |
| 2 | draw-call peak | ratchet **67** (budget 60) |
| 3 | blank frames | ratchet **1** |
| 4 | subject-in-frame | ratchet **6** |
| 5 | console asserts | **0**, absolute |

**Assertion 6 (reachability on the ordinary path) is NOT built** and says so in every report. A click-only E1→Close traversal is its own session. What exists is its first rung: the comfort run enters through the pre-fiction panel the way a player does, waiting out the 4 s ethics arm-delay and clicking *Log in*.

## What the first run found — `npm run audit` exits 1

1. **The scripted send dolly runs at 6.87 m/s and 141 °/s — 16× over.** A facet send targets Room 3; from Room 2 that is 8.87 m and 180° in 2.4 s. Worse than the 3.667 m/s fault that motivated the check. Latent — no beat fires the seam yet — and armed.
2. **The entrance descent is 1.2× over the law it is the source of:** 0.497 m/s. app.ts's comment claims 0.43; the same file's arithmetic (1.875 × 2.653 / 10) gives 0.497. Every player, every run, first thing.
3. **The entrance is the piece's draw-call peak at 67**, a leg S71 never measured (its 57 and 62 both reproduce exactly).
4. The blank check's own first false positive, caught and fixed: the sweep was photographing transition overlooks in states they never occur in.

**Nothing in the piece was retuned.** Exact durations are proposed (38.1 s / 24.5 s / 11.5 s) and not applied — both are pacing, and pacing is yours. The only src changes are the exported pose tables, a read-only `__camPose()` probe, and a `camMoveSeq` counter (a cut is not locomotion; without it the check would report thousands of m/s at every blink).

`npm test`, `tsc`, `npm run build` green; three consecutive audit runs give identical numbers. **A11 has still never run — every comfort figure is desktop-measured.** Nothing is committed.

Okay let go back to the narrative builds and check what is missing, that is most important part.

Modes: `audit` · `sweep` · `devices` · `sheet` · `blank` · `framing` · `comfort` · `verify` · `--help`. `blank` and `framing` are **offline** — they re-score a saved sweep with no browser at all (which is why the PNG reader is hand-written on `node:zlib`).

All three hardcoded things are parameterised. The third one mattered most: **the tool holds no camera numbers of its own.** [app.ts](src/engine/app.ts) exports `CAMERA_POSES`, [panel.ts](src/debug/panel.ts) publishes it as `window.__poses` under `?debug=1`, prop boxes come from `room-audit --boxes`. `puppeteer-core` is a devDependency and optional: no Chrome → skip, exit 0. `npm test` is untouched and still needs neither browser nor server.

## Cross-checks, before any number was believed

- projection vs the engine's own composed camera transform: **83 probes, 9.5 × 10⁻⁸ m**
- S71's `verify-aabb` folded into `shots.mjs verify`: **r4, 185 props, 0.00000 m**
- unplanned and strongest: the velocities **independently reproduce four figures three files measured by hand** — 0.415, 0.403/8.87°/s, 0.395, 0.121. Nothing was fitted to them.

## The five live assertions

| # | assertion | state |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | comfort envelope | **a LAW, fails outright** — 0.43 m/s / 9.1 °/s |
| 2 | draw-call peak | ratchet **67** (budget 60) |
| 3 | blank frames | ratchet **1** |
| 4 | subject-in-frame | ratchet **6** |
| 5 | console asserts | **0**, absolute |

**Assertion 6 (reachability on the ordinary path) is NOT built** and says so in every report. A click-only E1→Close traversal is its own session. What exists is its first rung: the comfort run enters through the pre-fiction panel the way a player does, waiting out the 4 s ethics arm-delay and clicking *Log in*.

## What the first run found — `npm run audit` exits 1

1. **The scripted send dolly runs at 6.87 m/s and 141 °/s — 16× over.** A facet send targets Room 3; from Room 2 that is 8.87 m and 180° in 2.4 s. Worse than the 3.667 m/s fault that motivated the check. Latent — no beat fires the seam yet — and armed.
2. **The entrance descent is 1.2× over the law it is the source of:** 0.497 m/s. app.ts's comment claims 0.43; the same file's arithmetic (1.875 × 2.653 / 10) gives 0.497. Every player, every run, first thing.
3. **The entrance is the piece's draw-call peak at 67**, a leg S71 never measured (its 57 and 62 both reproduce exactly).
4. The blank check's own first false positive, caught and fixed: the sweep was photographing transition overlooks in states they never occur in.

**Nothing in the piece was retuned.** Exact durations are proposed (38.1 s / 24.5 s / 11.5 s) and not applied — both are pacing, and pacing is yours. The only src changes are the exported pose tables, a read-only `__camPose()` probe, and a `camMoveSeq` counter (a cut is not locomotion; without it the check would report thousands of m/s at every blink).

`npm test`, `tsc`, `npm run build` green; three consecutive audit runs give identical numbers. **A11 has still never run — every comfort figure is desktop-measured.** Nothing is committed.

   turn. No menus, no confirmations, no "continue". The era is the only one where the piece moves

   thing off the hook — the player concludes "I would notice", and they would not. L is warm,
   competent, unhurried, genuinely pleasant. More patient than E1's counsellor, kinder than E3's

   RUN OUT: bring one thing it cannot place and L captions it wrong, twice, offers a third, then
